I'll draft batch 9 from the live FAIL rows and the existing batch format, then write only the plan, the script, and the rollback notes.Site policy for these rules is already in the handoff. I'll read Johnny's live PAM files before writing the script.Ubuntu’s `pam-auth-update` keeps `use_authtok` on the non-first password line, and `even_deny_root` turns on if the option is present at all. The batch will use profiles and leave that option commented.A failing check inside `if policy_files_ok` would keep going under `set -e`. Each check now returns immediately.## Detail

Batch 9 is a draft. Nothing in it has run on Johnny. The script is `docs/cis-fix/batch-9.sh`. The plan and the rollback are in `docs/cis-fix/batch-9.md`. The CSV was not touched.

Scope is the 20 failing 5.3 PAM rules plus four 5.4 rules that fit the same paste: `5.4.1.1` (max age 365), `5.4.1.5` (inactive 45), `5.4.3.2` (`TMOUT=900`), and `5.4.3.3` (umask `027`). Left for later: 1.4.1, 6.1.2.5, 3.2.7. No reboot.

Live state this evening, read-only: `libpam-pwquality` and `cracklib-runtime` are not installed. The apt lists already name `libpam-pwquality 1.4.5-5build1` and `cracklib-runtime 2.9.6-5.2build3`. `/usr/share/pam-configs` has only `capability`, `mkhomedir`, `systemd`, and `unix`. `common-auth` is `pam_unix.so nullok`. `common-password` is `pam_unix.so obscure yescrypt`. `faillock.conf` and `pwhistory.conf` have no active settings. `chage -l aj` still shows last change Oct 29, 2026, expire never, inactive never, max 99999. Four LAN SSH sessions were up from `192.168.50.223`.

The resolute `libpam-pwquality` package ships `/usr/share/pam-configs/pwquality` (priority 1024, `Default: yes`). `libpam-modules` ships the faillock and pwhistory modules and does not ship profiles for them, so the script adds five profiles and enables them with `pam-auth-update`. It does not hand-edit `common-auth`, `common-account`, or `common-password`.

`nullok` is removed by disabling the stock `unix` profile and enabling `johnny-unix`, which is that profile with both `nullok` tokens removed. The non-initial password line already contains `use_authtok`, and that is the line `pam-auth-update` uses once pwquality and pwhistory sit ahead of `pam_unix`. `use_authtok` is a module argument in `pam_pwhistory(8)` on Johnny and is not a key in `pwhistory.conf(5)`, so it is only on the profile line.

Faillock is three profiles so the generated stack is preauth (requisite, before `pam_unix`), authfail (after `pam_unix`, skipped on success because `success=end` is rewritten), and authsucc (additional block, after `pam_permit`, so a good login clears the counter). Account stack is `pam_faillock` then `pam_unix`. `deny = 5` and `unlock_time = 900`. On this PAM, `even_deny_root` is on when the option is present, so the script does not write `even_deny_root = off`. The stock comment stays, and an active `even_deny_root` or `root_unlock_time` is `STOP-active`.

Pwquality site values go in `/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/60-johnny-cis.conf` so the package conffile is not edited. `dictcheck` and `enforcing` stay at the default of 1.

Aging is `PASS_MAX_DAYS 365`, `useradd -D -f 45`, `chage -M 365 aj`, and `chage -I 45 aj`. There is no `chage -d`. PASTE 1 stops if the `chage -l` "Last password change" line moves. Oct 29 plus 365 days is still in the future, so `aj` is not forced to change the password now. Umask `027` is set in `login.defs` and in `/etc/profile.d/60-johnny-cis-shell.sh` because `USERGROUPS_ENAB yes` would turn a lone `UMASK 027` into `007`. That same file sets `readonly TMOUT=900`. Current shells do not pick it up until a new login.

Safety: at least two LAN SSH sessions before any change. One tar, `/root/batch9-pam-security.tar`, of `/etc/pam.d`, `/etc/security`, `/etc/login.defs`, and `/etc/default/useradd`, kept if it already exists. `passwd -S aj` is saved once. After the stack is written, the script checks module order, runs `sudo -n -v`, and checks the last-change line. Failure runs `/root/batch9-revert.sh` immediately. Success arms `johnny-cis-batch9-revert` for 300 seconds and prints `OK-batch-9-pending`. PASTE 1 does not disarm the timer.

PASTE 2 has to be a new SSH session: it reads `SSH_CONNECTION` from the process ancestry (sudo does not keep it) and stops if that client port was already in the peer list saved at the start of PASTE 1. It also requires `sudo -n -v` and an active timer, then stops the timer and runs `faillock --user aj --reset`.

PASTE 3 is KVM only. It stops the timer, restores the tar, disables the profiles this batch added, puts `chage` back from the saved `passwd -S` line, and resets faillock for `aj`. The revert does not remove the two installed packages. It disables the pwquality profile. `/etc/security/pwquality.conf` from the package may remain, unused.

How AJ runs it:

```bash
# RUNS ON: LAPTOP
# RUNS IN: LAPTOP
scp docs/cis-fix/batch-9.sh aj@192.168.50.152:cis-audit/batch-9.sh
```

```bash
# RUNS ON: JOHNNY (SSH)
# RUNS IN: SSH
# PASTE 1
sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-9.sh
```

Leave those sessions open, open a new SSH session, and within 300 seconds:

```bash
# RUNS ON: JOHNNY (SSH)
# RUNS IN: SSH
# PASTE 2
sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-9.sh 2
```

KVM only if sudo over SSH is already broken:

```bash
# RUNS ON: JOHNNY (KVM)
# RUNS IN: KVM
# PASTE 3
sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-9.sh 3
```

Assumption: a later `libpam-runtime` upgrade can enable the stock `unix` profile again. The revert path enables `unix` on purpose. Assumption: `pam-auth-update` will rewrite the stock `common-*` files without `--force` because they are still the packaged managed copies.

This needs Claude's review before AJ runs it.

## Relay

Batch 9 draft, not run. `docs/cis-fix/batch-9.sh` + plan/rollback in `docs/cis-fix/batch-9.md`. Scope: failing 5.3 PAM (pwquality, cracklib, faillock, pwhistory, nullok, use_authtok) and 5.4.1.1, 5.4.1.5, 5.4.3.2, 5.4.3.3. Not 1.4.1, 6.1.2.5, 3.2.7. No reboot.

Profiles via `pam-auth-update`, not hand-edits of `common-*`. `johnny-unix` replaces `unix` (nullok removed). faillock is preauth + authfail + authsucc. deny 5, unlock_time 900. `even_deny_root` left commented (present means on). `root_unlock_time` left commented. pwquality drop-in `pwquality.conf.d/60-johnny-cis.conf` (minlen 14, difok 2, maxrepeat 3, maxsequence 3, credits 0, enforce_for_root). pwhistory remember 24, enforce_for_root; `use_authtok` on the module line only. Aging: PASS_MAX_DAYS 365, INACTIVE 45, `chage -M/-I` only, stop if last-change date moves. TMOUT 900 and umask 027 in profile.d; UMASK 027 in login.defs.

Tar `/root/batch9-pam-security.tar` before changes. Validate includes `sudo -n -v`. 300s timer `johnny-cis-batch9-revert` restores pam.d+security and `faillock --user aj --reset`. PASTE 2 is a new SSH session (client port not in the saved peer list) and only then disarms. PASTE 3 is KVM, same revert. Needs review before AJ runs it.

## Outline

- Batch 9 draft, not applied
  - Script `docs/cis-fix/batch-9.sh`
  - Plan and rollback in `docs/cis-fix/batch-9.md`
  - CSV unchanged
- Scope
  - 20 failing 5.3 rules
  - 5.4.1.1, 5.4.1.5, 5.4.3.2, 5.4.3.3
  - Deferred: 1.4.1, 6.1.2.5, 3.2.7
  - No reboot
- Live state used
  - Packages absent; candidates already in the apt lists
  - Stock unix profile has nullok; non-initial password line already has use_authtok
  - aj last change Oct 29, 2026, max 99999, inactive off
  - Four LAN SSH sessions
- Method
  - pam-auth-update profiles, not common-* edits
  - johnny-unix replaces unix
  - faillock preauth / authfail / authsucc
  - even_deny_root and root_unlock_time stay commented
  - pwquality drop-in, not the package conffile
  - chage -M and -I only; stop if last-change line moves
  - umask 027 in login.defs and profile.d; TMOUT 900
- Safety
  - Two LAN SSH sessions required
  - Tar of pam.d, security, login.defs, useradd
  - sudo -n -v before the timer stays armed
  - 300s revert, including faillock --user aj --reset
  - PASTE 2 must be a new SSH session
  - PASTE 3 is KVM and runs the same revert
- Assumptions
  - A later libpam-runtime upgrade can re-enable stock unix
  - Stock common-* can be rewritten without --force
